preserved_objections.basis: Phosphorus-nitrogen interactions in BP/g-CN heterostructure are thermodynamically unstable in aqueous physiological conditions, leading to rapid degradation as documented in [doi:10.1038/s41598-026-42857-6] which shows black phosphorus degrades within hours in biological environments

The claimed 14-day continuous wear without recalibration is impossible given the mechanical stress from skin movement will cause delamination of the functionalization layer as acknowledged in the known failure modes, violating the boundary condition of mechanical stress from skin movement

[doi:10.1111/wrr.70194] demonstrates that protein adsorption on wearable sensors increases by 300-500% after 72 hours in wound environments, directly contradicting the 40% reduction claim without providing any experimental evidence for the proposed modification

Achieving uniform surface functionalization density at the nanoscale on a BP/g-CN heterostructure is technologically impossible with current manufacturing methods, as BP is extremely air-sensitive and cannot be processed in standard cleanroom environments

The testable prediction only measures protein adsorption after 72 hours but fails to specify which proteins are measured or under what mechanical conditions, making it impossible to validate the claim of reduced protein encapsulation attenuation over the full 14-day wear period
